item.title: How the Iran war threatens global food supply
item.summary: About a third of all fertilizer shipped globally passes through the Strait of Hormuz. Now shipping is all-but stopped through the Strait and this could have repercussions for the global food supply.

item.title: CBS News shutters its storied radio news service after nearly a century, ending an era
item.summary: The change is part of a round of layoffs at CBS News. When the radio service began operation in September 1927, it was a precursor to the entire CBS network. Today its top-of-the-hour news roundups are delivered to about 700 stations across the U.S.

item.title: Over 5,500 told to evacuate flooding in Hawaii as officials warn that dam could fail
item.summary: Muddy floodwaters from severe rains have inundated communities and prompted evacuation orders for more than 5,500 people in towns north of Honolulu. Officials are warning about the possible failure of a 120-year-old dam.

item.title: Why is the 'Bachelorette' canceled? A guide to the Taylor Frankie Paul controversy
item.summary: Taylor Frankie Paul rose to fame on The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives, then filmed a season of The Bachelorette. But it won't air as planned because of resurfaced domestic violence allegations.

item.title: With 'Arirang,' BTS returns to a K-pop moment of its own making
item.summary: Four years ago, the boy band went silent — but not before setting off a chain reaction that would reshape the pop market, conquer the Grammys and prime the world for an inevitable comeback.

item.title: Palestinians celebrate Eid in Gaza, making the most of a fragile ceasefire
item.summary: The ceasefire, in effect for the past six months, has brought some reprieve to Palestinians in Gaza despite continued hardship, displacement and Israeli restrictions on aid.

item.title: Jury finds Elon Musk misled investors during Twitter purchase
item.summary: A jury has found Elon Musk liable for misleading investors by deliberately driving down Twitter's stock price in the tumultuous months leading up to his 2022 acquisition of the social media company for $44 billion. But it absolved him of some fraud allegations.

item.title: The second death of Cesar Chavez and his legacy
item.summary: Accusations of sexual abuse by the famed union leader and champion of farmworker rights Cesar Chavez broke his legacy and those who admired him.

item.title: Epstein's former attorney testifies he had 'no knowledge whatsoever' of crimes
item.summary: Darren Indyke, longtime attorney for Jeffrey Epstein, testified he "did not know" of Epstein's sexual abuse of women and girls. He also confirmed the existence of hard drives held by Epstein's estate.

item.title: Martial arts star Chuck Norris dies at 86
item.summary: Norris karate chopped and kickboxed his way through more than a dozen action films, before leaping to TV in Walker, Texas Ranger.
